Ryan, 2026-08-26: 'modifiers often are reported entirely separately from cpt codes themselves (at least in claims data they are separate columns). Perhaps we just shouldn't mix CPT and modifiers together in any regexp.' The seven *.WITHMODIFIERS / *_MODIFIER rows all carry a |\w{2} alternative for the 2-char modifier, and THAT alternative is the entire flood - it matches any two word characters, measuring 340.5 per 10k chars of real article text. Splitting the two concerns fixes both halves: this row measures 0.14 per 10k, a 2,400x reduction, with 0 FALSE NEGATIVES over all 25,848 real 5-character CPT4+HCPCS concept_codes (CORRECTED 2026-08-27 from 25,850, re-measured against the OI build when the row's target was declared; 25,848 is also what the parent CPT4_HCPCS row records, so 25,850 was the outlier). The three branches are the three real shapes: 5 digits (99213), 4 digits + letter (0226T, CPT Category III), and letter + 4 digits (G0463 HCPCS, and M0201 which is a CPT code shaped like one). MODIFIERS ARE NOT DETECTABLE in free text and no pattern fixes that: 686 distinct two-character tokens including MG, AT, AA, AP, AS, US, CT, PT - enumerating all 686 as literals STILL measures 64.2 per 10k, because they are ordinary words. A suffix form code(?:[- ]?modifier)? was proposed, measured and REJECTED: 0 occurrences of a code followed by a two-char token across 25 papers, and it scored no better than this row. Do not reintroduce it without evidence from the literature. V-CPT and V-SRC are OHDSI-internal placeholders, not real codes, and are deliberately unmatched. 7-digit CPT chapter codes are out of scope per Ryan.
